headline: Ukraine should not join NATO
dek: Vance: 'Ukraine is not a member of NATO. I don't think they should be a member of NATO'; no formal US-Ukraine alliance; Ukraine should stop attacking Russian energy infrastructure because strikes on Russian diesel production raise energy prices for Americans.
sources: Vice President JD Vance, interview on 2WAY TONIGHT
fault_line: Is Ukraine defending itself — or raising YOUR energy prices?

sections.what_happened: Vance: 'Ukraine is not a member of NATO. I don't think they should be a member of NATO'; no formal US-Ukraine alliance; Ukraine should stop attacking Russian energy infrastructure because strikes on Russian diesel production raise energy prices for Americans. Washington will keep cooperating on other issues.
sections.what_verified: Four independent outlets (APA, Interfax-Ukraine, UNN, Censor.NET) quote identically; consistent with Trump's Newsmax criticism of refinery strikes resuming.
sections.what_disputed: Interfax notes NATO membership is Ukraine's stated long-term security demand; Vance frames as personal view ('as far as I know').
sections.why_matters: Pocketbook-first (demand playbook Tier 1): lead with what it costs the viewer, then the policy. Truth-side honesty: quote Vance verbatim, show Ukraine's stated NATO demand as counterpoint.
sections.context: Background: Vance 2WAY interview: Ukraine should not join NATO; must stop striking Russian energy facilities (pocketbook framing)
